emy|five.note: Boot 2009 '» 5 > hoʼ "five"' and the syllabic '» ho-ho-ho > hoʼ'; Kettunen & Helmke numeral table '5 hoʼ'. Hieroglyphically attested. Row confirmed Classic Maya, not a mislabelled modern wordlist: its pronouns hiin and hat exist only in the glyphic corpus and match none of the atlas's yua/quc/ctu/itz rows.

emy|good.note: Boot 2009 '» ʼu-tzi > utz "good"'; K&H 'utz | yu-tzi | y-utz | adj'. utz is the EPIGRAPHIC spelling, not modern ALMG — the orthographic suspicion that raised this flag was wrong. Row confirmed Classic Maya, not a mislabelled modern wordlist: its pronouns hiin and hat exist only in the glyphic corpus and match none of the atlas's yua/quc/ctu/itz rows.

emy|mother.note: Kettunen & Helmke 'naʼ | na | na[ʼ] | n | "lady, mother"'. Attested. Row confirmed Classic Maya, not a mislabelled modern wordlist: its pronouns hiin and hat exist only in the glyphic corpus and match none of the atlas's yua/quc/ctu/itz rows.

emy|one.note: Boot 2009 '» 1 > jun "one"' with his n.91 on the later jun>hun merger; K&H numeral table '1 jun'. Attested. Row confirmed Classic Maya, not a mislabelled modern wordlist: its pronouns hiin and hat exist only in the glyphic corpus and match none of the atlas's yua/quc/ctu/itz rows.

emy|water.note: Boot 2009 'ta HAʼ > ta haʼ "in water"', 'SAK-HAʼ'; K&H 'haʼ | ha-a | n'. The h/j split this row shows (haʼ, hoʼ vs jun) IS the Classic convention; Boot and K&H both print haʼ, not jaʼ. Row confirmed Classic Maya, not a mislabelled modern wordlist: its pronouns hiin and hat exist only in the glyphic corpus and match none of the atlas's yua/quc/ctu/itz rows.

juc|i.note: Manchu proxy, now declared as such in wordEvidence. Grube's pronoun sketch gives the corpus's COMPLETE inventory — mini (1sg gen./poss.), two demonstratives, one indefinite — and there is no bi. Verified: no entry in Grube is glossed 'ich'. The agreement with p_tun *bi is because Proto-Tungusic is built on Manchu, not because the cell was copied from the proto row. Unchecked against Kane 1989 (JurchenB), which is not reachable online.

juc|iron.note: Grube 1896 glossary #574: 'seh-leh, Eisen. 574. m. sele.' Attested in the 女真譯語, and this row writes Grube's Manchu column by convention. Verified in Grube's own text 2026-09-20.

juc|three.note: Grube 1896 #638: 'i-lan, drei. 638. m. ilan.' Attested. Same convention as juc|iron.

juc|you.note: Manchu proxy, declared. See juc|i: no 2sg pronoun in Grube's corpus, and no entry glossed 'du'.

pyx|star.note: leak, known and accepted for now. Declared evidence: inferred, source Tibeto-Burman comparative (*s-kar) — the cell says what it is, which is why review 546 left it standing while emptying the eleven that claimed direct attestation. kar· does occur twice in the corpus (inscription 027) but no source glosses it. pyx|you.note: leak, known and accepted for now. Declared evidence: inferred, source Tibeto-Burman comparative (*naŋ). naṅ· occurs once (inscription 178), unglossed. Same open policy question as pyx|star. Note obr|you holds the identical form and IS attested.

Wikipedia's Khitan table gives s.ia/s.en and says it CORRESPONDS TO Mongolian sayin — the comparandum printed beside the Khitan word was taken for the word. Byte-identical to pmng *sajin. zkt|i.note: LEAK, and the cell should be EMPTY. Khitan personal pronouns are essentially unread: Kane's glossary has none, and Wu & Róna-Tas 2019 (AOH 72/1: 58) say glyph <bi> (225) 'is used only in transcription of Chinese' per Kane K62. The only pronoun the field has is <bod> 'body, oneself', tentatively 3sg, identified in 2017. Not yet emptied; see the zkt row audit in dev-handoff.
